question: Which type of tree is dominant in temperate forests?
support: Figure 44.18 Deciduous trees are the dominant plant in the temperate forest. (credit: Oliver Herold).

question: What are the two most common silicates?
support: Feldspar and quartz are the two most common silicates. In beryl, the silicate pyramids join together as rings. Biotite is mica. It can be broken apart into thin, flexible sheets. Compare the beryl and the biotite shown in Figure below .

question: What term means the amount of water vapor in the air?
support: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air. High humidity increases the chances of clouds and precipitation.

question: Upon death of an organism, during composition, what returns to the soil as ammonium ions?
support: When organisms die and decompose, their nitrogen is returned to the soil as ammonium ions. Nitrifying bacteria change some of the ammonium ions into nitrates.

question: Chemical reactions involve a transfer of heat energy. measured in what?
support: Chemical reactions involve a transfer of heat energy. Measured in joules.

question: The lens focuses light on the retina , which covers the back of the inside of the eye. the retina has light-sensing photoreceptor cells called?
support: The lens focuses light on the retina , which covers the back of the inside of the eye. The retina has light-sensing photoreceptor cells called rods and cones. Rods let us see in dim light. Cones let us detect light of different colors.

question: What type of bonds are formed by the side-to-side overlap of p orbitals?
support: Sigma bonds are formed by the end-to-end overlap of bonding orbitals. Pi bonds are formed by the side-to-side overlap of p orbitals. Single bonds are normally sigma bonds. A double or triple bond consists of one sigma bond and either one or two pi bonds.

question: During the first year after birth, what is a baby called?
support: For the first year after birth, a baby is called an infant. Childhood begins at age two and continues until adolescence. Adolescence is the last stage of life before adulthood.

question: What is the adaptation that certain animals use to become less visible to predators and prey?
support: Camouflage by the dead leaf mantis makes it less visible to both its predators and prey. If alarmed, it lies motionless on the rainforest floor of Madagascar, Africa, camouflaged among the actual dead leaves. It eats other animals up to the size of small lizards.

question: Childbirth usually starts when which sac breaks?
support: During childbirth , a baby passes from the uterus, through the vagina, and out of the mother’s body. Childbirth usually starts when the amniotic sac breaks.

question: What is the term for when an embryo fixes itself to the side of the uterus?
support: Implantation occurs when the developing embryo fixes itself to the side of the uterus.

question: What type of plants does human welfare depend greatly on?
support: 30.4 Human welfare depends greatly on seed plants.

question: Bones, cartilage, and what other thing make up the skeletal system?
support: Bones, cartilage, and ligaments make up the skeletal system.

question: Where do mushrooms get their energy?
support: Mushrooms gain their energy from decomposing dead organisms. Explain why a mushroom is not a plant.

question: The ileum is the last part of what digestive system organ?
support: The ileum is the last part of the small intestine. It is covered with villi like the jejunum. A few remaining nutrients are absorbed in the ileum. From the ileum, any remaining food waste passes into the large intestine.

question: A diagram in which the numerical values of variables are represented by the height or length of lines or rectangles of equal width is called?
support: Bar graphs are especially useful for comparing values for different types of things. The bar graph in Figure below shows the number of vehicles of each type that passed the checkpoint.

question: Vultures, raccoons and blowflies are examples of what?
support: Scavengers consume the soft tissues of dead animals. Examples of scavengers include vultures, raccoons, and blowflies.

question: What three parts is the earth divided into?
support: From outside to inside, Earth is divided into crust, mantle, and core. Each has a different chemical makeup. Earth can also be divided into layers with different properties. The two most important are lithosphere and asthenosphere.

question: In physics, when one subtracts the frictional force from the applied force what is the result?
support: The net force is found by subtracting the frictional force from the applied force.

question: Digestive enzymes are released, or secreted, by the organs of which body system?
support: Digestive enzymes are released, or secreted, by the organs of the digestive system. These enzymes include proteases that digest proteins, and nucleases that digest nucleic acids. Examples of digestive enzymes are:.

question: What part of the male reproductive system is involved with the most common disorders?
support: Most common disorders of the male reproductive system involve the testes. They include injuries and cancer.

question: What gas is released when dead organisms and other organic materials decompose?
support: Carbon dioxide is given off when dead organisms and other organic materials decompose.

question: What type of lens is thicker at the edges than it is in the middle?
support: A concave lens is thicker at the edges than it is in the middle. This causes rays of light to diverge. The light forms a virtual image that is right-side up and smaller than the object.

question: Lenses that focus light are called what?
support: Lenses , made from curved pieces of glass, focus or de-focus light as it passes through. Lenses that focus light are called converging lenses, and these are the ones used to make telescopes and cameras. Lenses that de-focus light are called diverging lenses.

question: What makes up the dense outer layer of bones?
support: Compact bone makes up the dense outer layer of bone. It is very hard and strong.

question: All of the elements in group 9 have nine of which electrons?
support: All of the elements in group 9 have nine valence electrons.

question: Surging hormones will cause adolescents to have what?
support: Adolescents may have mood swings because of surging hormones .

question: What cells does the skeletal system make?
support: The skeletal system makes blood cells. Most blood cells are produced inside certain types of bones.

question: Traits may also be controlled by multiple alleles or multiple what?
support: Inheritance is more complex for traits in which there is codominance or incomplete dominance. Traits may also be controlled by multiple alleles or multiple genes. Many traits are influenced by the environment as well.

question: Silver is an example of a mineral containing only one kind of what?
support: All minerals have a definite chemical makeup. A few minerals are made of only one kind of element. Silver is a mineral made only of silver atoms. Diamond and graphite are both made only of the element carbon.

question: Where are liverworts most often found?
support: Liverworts have two distinct appearances: they can either be leafy like mosses or flattened and ribbon-like. Liverworts get their name from the type with the flattened bodies, which can resemble a liver ( Figure below ). Liverworts can often be found along stream beds.

question: What is the side to side movement of the mandible called?
support: Excursion Excursion is the side to side movement of the mandible. Lateral excursion moves the mandible away from the midline, toward either the right or left side. Medial excursion returns the mandible to its resting position at the midline.

question: Ecological succession refers to the change in the numbers and types of species that live in what groups?
support: Communities are not usually static. The numbers and types of species that live in them generally change over time. This is called ecological succession . Important cases of succession are primary and secondary succession.

question: Salicylic acid is used in the synthesis of acetylsalicylic acid, or more commonly called?
support: Salicylic acid is used in the synthesis of acetylsalicylic acid, or aspirin. One gram dissolves in 460 mL of water to create a saturated solution with a pH of 2.40.

question: Type 1 diabetes and gigantism are examples of what type of disorder?
support: Endocrine system diseases are fairly common. An endocrine disease usually involves the secretion of too much or not enough hormone by an endocrine hormone. Examples of endocrine diseases are gigantism and Type 1 diabetes.

question: What is a reptiles skin covered in to protect them from drying out?
support: The cell cycle is a repeating series of events that cells go through. It includes growth, DNA synthesis, and cell division. In eukaryotic cells, there are two growth phases, and cell division includes mitosis.

question: Two smaller isotopes, more neutrons, and heat energy are the products of what type of reaction?
support: Nuclear fission reactions involve collision of a slow neuron with an element, usually uranium. The products of a fission reaction are two smaller isotopes, more neutrons, and heat energy.

question: What structures are at the end of the long air passages in the lungs?
support: During respiration, oxygen gets pulled into the lungs and enters the blood by passing across the thin alveoli membranes and into the capillaries. The alveoli are at the end of the long air passages.

question: What is a disease caused by the same virus that causes chicken pox?
support: Shingles. Shingles is a disease caused by the same virus that causes chicken pox.

question: Matter is made up of a mixture of things called what?
support: Matter is made up of a mixture of things called elements. Elements are substances that cannot be broken down into simpler substances. There are more than 100 known elements, and 92 occur naturally around us. The others have been made only in the laboratory.

question: Water seeps into the ground through permeable material and stops when it reaches what?
support: Water seeps into the ground through permeable material and stops when it reaches an impermeable rock. Predict the purpose of the well in the diagram.

question: Sponges exemplify what type of arrangement, where different cells are specialized for different functions, but each cell works alone?
support: Sponges have cell-level organization, in which different cells are specialized for different functions, but each cell works alone. For example, some cells digest food, while other cells let water pass through the sponge.

question: What process is used for cell growth, repair of cuts and replacement of worn out cells?
support: Yes, just like this car, cells cannot last forever. Cells do eventually wear out. At that point, they need to be replaced. This is one reason that your cells divide. New cells that result after cells divide are also used for growth and to repair cuts.

question: What is a form of cell division in prokaryotic organisms that produces identical offspring?
support: Binary fission is a form of cell division in prokaryotic organisms that produces identical offspring.

question: What do ionic bonds form between?
support: Ionic bonds form only between metals and nonmetals. That’s because metals “want” to give up electrons, and nonmetals “want” to gain electrons.

question: What type of telescopes collect and focus radio waves from distant objects?
support: Radio telescopes collect and focus radio waves from distant objects.

question: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction that gets its energy from what?
support: One of the most important series of endothermic reactions is photosynthesis. The energy needed for photosynthesis comes from light.

question: Paramecium possess tiny hair-like cilia that help them do what?
support: Some protists, like these Paramecium , act much like animals. Notice the tiny hair-like cilia that help them move. The food vacuoles, where they digest their prey, are colored in orange.

question: In both eukaryotes and prokaryotes, ribosomes are the non-membrane bound organelles where what main product of the cell is made?
support: In both eukaryotes and prokaryotes, ribosomes are the non-membrane bound organelles where proteins are made. Ribosomes are like the machines in the factory that produce the factory's main product. Proteins are the main product of the cell.

question: Cells that have a nucleus and other organelles which are membrane-bound are generally called what kinds of cells?
support: Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. This allows these cells to have complex functions.

question: What is first stage of cellular respiration?
support: The first stage of cellular respiration is glycolysis . It does not require oxygen, and it does not take place in the mitochondrion - it takes place in the cytosol of the cytoplasm.

question: Can nematodes be a parasite of plants, animals, or both?
support: Nematodes can be parasites of plants and animals.

question: The similarities and differences between the genomes confirm patterns of what?
support: The similarities and differences between the genomes confirm patterns of evolution.

question: Viruses replicate only in where?
support: 19.2 Viruses replicate only in host cells.

question: What does pepsin help break down into amino acids?
support: Pepsin, produced in the stomach. Pepsin helps break down proteins into amino acids.

question: In many places, small hills rise above the ocean floor. these hills are undersea volcanoes, called what?
support: The ocean floor is not totally flat. In many places, small hills rise above the ocean floor. These hills are undersea volcanoes, called seamounts ( Figure above ). Some rise more than 1000 m above the seafloor.

question: The medium moves back and forth in the same direction as the wave in what type of wave?
support: In a longitudinal wave, the medium moves back and forth in the same direction as the wave.

question: Invertebrates (and higher animals) can also be placed in one of two groups based on how they develop as what?
support: Eight invertebrate phyla contain most invertebrate species. Invertebrates (and higher animals) can also be placed in one of two groups based on how they develop as embryos.

question: What are the specialized cells that sponges have?
support: Sponges have specialized cells called collar cells. Describe how collar cells are specialized for the functions they serve.

question: What are the small molecules or proteins produced by bacteria that regulate gene expression?
support: Figure 9.17 Autoinducers are small molecules or proteins produced by bacteria that regulate gene expression.

question: What navigation technology works on the same principle as echolocation?
support: Sonar works on the same principle as echolocation.

question: What is the most direct way of recovering a metal from its ores?
support: Electrolysis is the most direct way of recovering a metal from its ores. However, the Na (aq)/Na(s), 2+.

question: What is the term used to describe the minerals and vitamins that are not needed for providing the body with energy but are still essential for good health?
support: Micronutrients are nutrients the body needs in relatively small amounts. They include minerals and vitamins. These nutrients don’t provide the body with energy, but they are still essential for good health.

question: What do you call a quantity of motion that has both size as well as direction?
support: Direction is just as important as distance in describing motion. A vector is a quantity that has both size and direction. It can be used to represent the distance and direction of motion.

question: What process done by bacteria makes them important producers in aquatic ecosystems?
support: type of bacteria that carry out photosynthesis and are important producers in aquatic ecosystems.

question: What is the the process by which remains or traces of living things become fossils called?
support: The process by which remains or traces of living things become fossils is called fossilization ( Figure below ). Most fossils are preserved in sedimentary rocks.

question: Quarks are very tiny particles of matter that make up what?
support: Quarks are even tinier particles of matter that make up protons and neutrons. Scientists have identified six different types of quarks.

question: The right and left hip bones, with the addition of the sacrum and coccyx form what section of the skeleton?
support: Figure 8.12 Pelvis The pelvic girdle is formed by a single hip bone. The hip bone attaches the lower limb to the axial skeleton through its articulation with the sacrum. The right and left hip bones, plus the sacrum and the coccyx, together form the pelvis.

question: Does lava flow quickly or slowly when thick?
support: When lava is thick, it flows slowly. If thick lava makes it to the surface, it cannot flow far from the vent. It often stays right in the middle of a crater at the top of a volcano. Here the lava creates a large, round lava dome ( Figure below ).

question: Habitat loss caused by human actions is a prime culprit in what phenomenon, which appears to be occurring for a sixth time?
support: Evidence shows that a sixth mass extinction is occurring. The single biggest cause is habitat loss caused by human actions. There are many steps you can take to help protect biodiversity. For example, you can use less energy.

question: All of the petals together are called what?
support: All of the petals ( Figure below ) together are called the corolla . They are bright and colorful to attract a particular pollinator , an animal that carries pollen from one flower to another. Examples of pollinators include birds and insects.

question: What color is phosphate mineral turquoise?
support: Turquoise is a phosphate mineral with a beautiful blue color. The stone is not as rare as some minerals and is commonly used for jewelry.

question: Plants go through seasonal changes after detecting differences in what?
support: Plants go through seasonal changes after detecting differences in day length.

question: What symbol is used to indicate directionality in chemical reactions?
support: The arrow (→) shows the direction in which the reaction occurs. In many reactions, the reaction also occurs in the opposite direction. This is represented with another arrow pointing in the opposite direction (←).

question: What are the most diverse organisms on earth, which are often classified by shape or how they react to gram stain?
support: Bacteria are the most diverse organisms on Earth. They are often classified by shape or how they react to Gram stain.

question: Lymph vessels make up a circulatory system that is similar to the blood vessels of what system?
support: Lymph vessels make up a circulatory system that is similar to the blood vessels of the cardiovascular system. However, lymph vessels circulate lymph instead of blood, and the heart does not pump lymph through the vessels.

question: What process takes place when plants release water vapor through pores in their leaves called stomata?
support: Transpiration takes place when plants release water vapor through pores in their leaves called stomata.

question: Like the platypus, the echnida is a what?
support: Echidna. Like the platypus, the echnida is a monotreme. The only living monotreme species inhabit Australia and New Guinea.

question: What is an adaptation?
support: Adaptations are favorable traits that organisms inherit. Adaptations develop from variations within a population and help organisms to survive in their given environment.

question: Population size is the number of what in a population?
support: Population size is the number of individuals in a population.

question: What type of reactions absorb heat from their surroundings?
support: Endothermic reactions absorb heat from their surroundings.

question: What is part of a large fungus that lives underground?
support: Mushrooms aren't around just so you can put them on your pizza. The mushroom is part of a large fungus that lives underground. The mushroom develops above the ground when the fungus is ready to reproduce.

question: In the inner ear, the vibrations are changed to electrical signals by hair cells lining what?
support: In the inner ear, the vibrations are changed to electrical signals by hair cells lining the cochlea. The electrical signals then travel to the brain.

question: Angiosperm seed develops inside of what?
support: In gymnosperms, a seed develops on the scale of a cone. Only an angiosperm seed develops inside an ovary.

question: The efficiency of a machine is a measure of how well it reduces what force?
support: The efficiency of a machine is a measure of how well it reduces friction. It is calculated as the percent of input work that becomes output work.

question: What happens to energy when work is done by a system?
support: Work done on a system puts energy into it. Work done by a system removes energy from it. Give an example for each statement. When solving for speed in Example 7.4, we kept only the positive root. Why?.

question: Parasites infect the host's what?
support: Plasmodium protozoa cause malaria . The parasites are spread by a mosquito vector. Parasites enter a host’s blood through the bite of an infected mosquito. The parasites infect the host’s red blood cells, causing symptoms such as fever, joint pain, anemia, and fatigue.

question: Evaporation of moisture is greatest where it is?
support: Evaporation of moisture is greatest where it is hot and sunny. Therefore, cold climates with low precipitation may not be as dry as warm climates with the same amount of precipitation.

question: Where does most of the earth's energy come from?
support: Almost all energy on Earth comes from the Sun. The Sun’s energy heats the planet and the air around it. Sunlight also powers photosynthesis and life on Earth.

question: What causes the alpine tundra to be so cold?
support: Alpine tundra climates occur at high altitudes at any latitude. They are also called highland climates. These regions are very cold because they are so far above sea level. The alpine tundra climate is very similar to the polar tundra climate.

question: What is the name of the complex mixture that consists of water, proteins, fats, carbohydrates, and minerals?
support: Milk is a complex mixture of water, proteins, fats, carbohydrates, and minerals. While the minerals and carbohydrates are water-soluble, the fats and some of the proteins do not dissolve but are held in suspension.

question: What is the term for an exact genetic copy?
support: Recombinant DNA technology is used in gene cloning. A clone is an exact genetic copy. Genes are cloned for many reasons, including use in medicine and in agriculture.

question: Where do recent rocks point towards on earth?
support: Rocks on different continents that are the same age point to different locations. Only recent rocks point to the current north magnetic pole.

question: What do charged particles in motion generate?
support: Paints can be both toxic and flammable. Paints may spill on the ground or be thrown improperly in the trash.

question: The concentration of the hydrogen ion in a solution can be calculated when what is known?
support: When the pH of a solution is known, the concentration of the hydrogen ion can be calculated. The inverse of the logarithm (or antilog) is the 10 x key on a calculator.

question: Vascular plants all have roots, stems, and what?
support: Vascular plants also have roots, stems, and leaves.

question: What indicates the speed at which a reaction proceeds?
support: The reaction rate indicates how fast the reaction proceeds.

question: What are plant structures that contain male and/or female reproductive organs?
support: Some seed plants evolved another major adaptation. This was the formation of seeds in flowers. Flowers are plant structures that contain male and/or female reproductive organs.

question: What is the name of the first stage of photosynthesis?
support: The first stage of photosynthesis is called the light reactions. During this stage, light is absorbed and transformed to chemical energy in the bonds of NADPH and ATP. You can follow the process in the Figure below as you read about it below.

question: What do you call nutrients that your body needs in fairly large amounts?
support: Macronutrients are nutrients the body needs in relatively large amounts. They include carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and water.

question: Vivipary refers to the development and nourishment of a what?
support: Vivipary refers to the development and nourishment of an embryo within the mother’s body. Birth may be followed by a period of parental care of the offspring. This reproductive strategy occurs in almost all mammals.

question: What are the two main types of star clusters?
support: The two main types of star clusters are open clusters and globular clusters.

question: The three units of kpa, atm or mmhg commonly measure what?
support: Bone: Christopher Auyeung; Tonsils: User:Klem/Wikimedia Commons; Spleen: Henry Gray; Thymus: User:LearnAnatomy/Wikipedia. Each lymph organ has a different job in the immune system . Bone: CC-BY-NC-SA 3.0; Tonsils and Thymus: CC-BY 3.0; Spleen: Public Domain.

question: While the goal of science is to increase knowledge, the goal of what is to use knowledge for practical purposes?
support: Technology is sometimes referred to as applied science, but it has a different goal than science. The goal of science is to increase knowledge. The goal of technology is to use knowledge for practical purposes.

question: What are the two terms that designate how well aqueous solutions conduct electricity?
support: Aqueous solutions can be classified as polar or nonpolar depending on how well they conduct electricity.

question: Honeybees doing the waggle dance or spiders spinning a web are examples of what type of behavior?
support: Examples of innate behavior include honeybees doing the waggle dance or spiders spinning a web.

question: What glands remove water, salts and other wastes from skin?
support: Skin Sweat glands remove water, salts, and other wastes. Integumentary system.

question: The percent yield is determined by calculating the ratio of actual yield by what?
support: The percent yield is determined by calculating the ratio of actual yield/theoretical yield.

question: What happens to water when it freezes?
support: In its pure liquid form, water is a poor conductor of electricity. Unlike most substances, water is more dense in its liquid state than its solid state. As a result, water expands when it freezes, and ice floats on water.

question: In humans, fertilization occurs soon after the oocyte leaves this?
support: Figure 43.18 In humans, fertilization occurs soon after the oocyte leaves the ovary. Implantation occurs eight or nine days later. (credit: Ed Uthman).

question: What refers to the ability to change or move matter and is required by all life processes and living things?
support: Energy is the ability to change or move matter. All life processes require energy, so all living things need energy.

question: What do you call a chemical process used to treat water by destroying a contaminant?
support: Chemical remediation can also treat water in the aquifer. A chemical is pumped into the aquifer. The chemical destroys the contaminant.

question: Assume a molecule must cross the plasma membrane into what?
support: 5. Assume a molecule must cross the plasma membrane into a cell. The molecule is a very large protein. How will it be transported into the cell? Explain your answer.

question: Fahrenheit, celsius, and kelvin are all units which measure what?
support: There are three temperature scales that are commonly used. Their units are °F (degrees Fahrenheit), °C (degrees Celsius), and K (Kelvin).

question: What is the purpose of a bird using flashy displays?
support: Birds often use flashy displays to attract mates.

question: What do you call the ancient cores of continents, where the earliest continental crust is now found?
support: The earliest continental crust is now found in the ancient cores of continents, called the cratons . Geologists can learn many things about the Precambrian by studying the rocks of the cratons.

question: A frameshift mutation is a deletion or insertion of one or more of what that changes the reading frame of the base sequence?
support: A frameshift mutation is a deletion or insertion of one or more nucleotides that changes the reading frame of the base sequence. Deletions remove nucleotides, and insertions add nucleotides. Consider the following sequence of bases in RNA:.

question: What is an area of land called that is wet for all or part of the year?
support: A wetland is an area that is wet for all or part of the year. Wetlands are home to certain types of plants.

question: What can refer to a rope in a particular shape and a genetic structure involved in splicing?
support: A lariat can refer to a rope in the form of a lasso. But it is also a genetic structure involved in splicing.

question: What is the term for the use of technology to treat genetic disorders or change organisms so they are more useful to people?
support: Biotechnology is the use of technology to treat genetic disorders or change organisms so they are more useful to people. Methods include gene cloning. Applications include gene therapy and genetically modified food crops.

question: What type of tissue makes up the brain and the nerves that connect the brain to all parts of the body?
support: Nervous tissue is made up of neurons, or nerve cells, that carry electrical messages. Nervous tissue makes up the brain and the nerves that connect the brain to all parts of the body.

question: What does the pull of the moon's gravity on earth cause?
support: Figure below shows why tides occur. The main cause of tides is the pull of the Moon’s gravity on Earth. The pull is greatest on whatever is closest to the Moon. Although the gravity pulls the land, only the water can move. As a result:.

question: What force makes objects seem lighter in water?
support: Because of buoyant force, objects seem lighter in water. You may have noticed this when you went swimming and could easily pick up a friend or sibling under the water. Some of the person’s weight was countered by the buoyant force of the water.

question: What are hydrocarbons most important use?
support: Hydrocarbons have a wide variety of important uses, but their most important use is as fuels.

question: The protein without the prosthetic group is known as the what?
support: As we will return to later, proteins are functional entities, composed of polypeptides and prosthetic group. The prosthetic group is essential for normal protein function. The protein without the prosthetic group is known as the apoprotein. biofundamentals – coreBIO.

question: What do different soil horizons show different amounts of?
support: Soil horizons are layers within a soil. Different soil horizons show different amounts of alteration.

question: What do you call air flowing over earth’s surface?
support: Air always flows from an area of higher pressure to an area of lower pressure. Air flowing over Earth’s surface is called wind . The greater the difference in pressure, the stronger the wind blows.

question: Research that focuses on understanding basic properties and processes without concern for the usefulness of this understanding is known as what kind of research?
support: Pure research focuses on understanding basic properties and processes.

question: Beta decay occurs when a nucleus has too few of what relative to protons?
support: Beta decay occurs when a nucleus is unstable because it has too many or too few neutrons relative to protons. The nucleus emits a beta particle and energy. A beta particle is either an electron (beta-minus decay) or a positron (beta-plus decay).

question: Trees have woody stems covered with what?
support: Trees have woody stems covered with bark.

question: Esters can be formed by heating carboxylic acids and alcohols in the presence of?
support: Esters can be formed by heating carboxylic acids and alcohols in the presence of an acid catalyst. This process is reversible, and the starting materials can be regenerated by reacting an ester with water in the presence of a weak base.

question: Displacement is the separation between a beginning position and what other place?
support: The separation between original and final position is called displacement.

question: What is the term for the long-time average of weather?
support: Climate is the long-term average of weather.

question: Food allergies, ulcers, and heartburn all affect what organ system?
support: Many diseases can affect the digestive system. Three of the most common diseases that affect the digestive system are food allergies, ulcers, and heartburn. Foodborne illnesses and food intolerance are also serious issues associated with the digestive system.

question: What are formed by the loss of one or two electrons from an element?
support: Cations are formed by the loss of one or two electrons from an element.

question: In which ways may sponges reproduce?
support: The sponge life cycle includes sexual reproduction. Sponges may also reproduce asexually.

question: What do barnacles anchor to?
support: Mo Riza. Barnacles are adapted to the intertidal zone by anchoring to rocks . CC BY 2.0.

question: The relative sizes of the atoms show several trends with regard to what visual method of organization?
support: The relative sizes of the atoms show several trends with regard to the structure of the periodic table. Atoms become larger going down a column and smaller going across a period.

question: How do endocrine hormones travel throughout the body?
support: Endocrine hormones travel throughout the body in the blood. However, each endocrine hormone affects only certain cells, called target cells.

question: The post-anal tail is at the end of the organism opposite what?
support: The post-anal tail is at the end of the organism opposite the head. It extends beyond the anus.

question: Active transport moves substances from an area of lower concentration to an area of?
support: Active transport requires energy because it moves substances from an area of lower to higher concentration. An example is the sodium-potassium pump. Another form of active transport is vesicle transport, which is needed for very large molecules.

question: How does the skin eliminates excess water and salts?
support: The skin eliminates excess water and salts in sweat.

question: What reaction, along with photosynthesis, provides energy to the vast majority of living things?
support: The chemical reactions of photosynthesis and cellular respiration together provide energy to virtually all living things on Earth.

question: Where do physical laws govern energy flow and chemical cycling?
support: 55.1 Physical laws govern energy flow and chemical cycling in ecosystems.

question: Earthquakes occur most often at which natural feature?
support: The vast majority of earthquakes happen at plate boundaries.

question: How many atmospheric circulation cells are there?
support: The globe has six atmospheric circulation cells. Three are north of the Equator and three are south. These cells have names.

question: Where is the youngest seafloor located?
support: The youngest seafloor is at the ridge. The oldest is farthest from the ridge. The oldest seafloor is much younger than the oldest continent.

question: What delivers natural gas from rock that might not otherwise be obtainable?
support: Fracking delivers natural gas from rock that might not otherwise be obtainable.

question: Permanent dipole-dipole interactions are found in what kind of molecules?
support: Polar molecules have permanent dipole-dipole interactions.

question: In projectile motion, the horizontal displacement of an object is called its what?
support: In projectile motion, the horizontal displacement of an object is called its range .

question: What type of engine burns fuel to heat water and produce steam?
support: An external combustion engine burns fuel to heat water and produce steam. The steam is under pressure and is used to push a piston back and forth inside a cylinder. As the piston moves back and forth, it moves a piston rod, which can do work.

question: Reactants are substances that start what?
support: Reactants are substances that start a chemical reaction.

question: Stoichiometry is concerned with the reactants and the products in chemical what?
support: numerical relationships between the reactants and the products in balanced chemical reactions is called stoichiometry.

question: What do you call the angle at which waves strike a wall?
support: Waves strike a wall at an angle, called the angle of incidence. The waves are reflected at the same angle, called the angle of reflection, but in a different direction. Both angles are measured relative to a line that is perpendicular to the wall.

question: What term refers to the amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature?
support: Solubility is the amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature. Some solutes have greater solubility than others.

question: What are the outer planets of the solar system made of?
support: The inner planets are small and rocky, while the outer planets are large and made of gases. Why might the planets have formed into these two groups?.

question: Deer, rabbits and mice are an example of what link between producers and other consumers?
support: Herbivores consume producers such as plants or algae. They are a necessary link between producers and other consumers. Examples include deer, rabbits, and mice.

question: What type of virus is the flu caused by?
support: Doesn't look like fun. The flu is caused by an influenza virus. And usually a slightly different virus every season.

question: Peristalsis is necessary for what basic bodily function?
support: Describe peristalsis, and explain why it is necessary for digestion.

question: Force is a vector because it has what two things?
support: Force is a vector because it has both size and direction. Like other vectors, it can be represented by an arrow.

question: What is the last step in scientific investigation?
support: The last step in a scientific investigation is the communication of results with others.

question: What instrument is used to make objects in space appear closer?
support: Telescopes made objects in space seem closer. But they didn't make it any easier to visit them. Human space flight required something entirely different: rockets.

question: Water is composed of which two elements?
support: Water is a binary compound composed of hydrogen and oxygen. The hydrogen and oxygen gases produced in the reaction are both diatomic molecules.

question: All the members of a species that live in the same area form a what?
support: All the members of a species that live in the same area form a population . Many different species live together in an ecosystem. All their populations make up a community . What populations live together in the grassland pictured below ( Figure above )?.

question: New species may be created by natural selection and one other way. what is the other way?
support: Speciation, the creation of a new species, can happen through natural selection or artificial selection.

question: About how many years ago did our solar system begin?
support: Our solar system began about 5 billion years ago. The Sun, planets and other solar system objects all formed at about the same time.

question: How many colors of light can the human eye detect?
support: The human eye can detect only three colors of light. What three colors are they? How can we perceive other colors of light?.

question: What part is written first when naming an ionic compound?
support: Ionic compounds are named by writing the name of the cation followed by the name of the anion.

question: What work by lowering the activation energy of reactions and are needed to speed up chemical reactions in organisms?
support: Enzymes are needed to speed up chemical reactions in organisms. They work by lowering the activation energy of reactions.

question: Special cell in the epidermis of the skin that produces the brown pigment called what?
support: special cell in the epidermis of the skin that produces the brown pigment called melanin.

question: Burning fossil fuels releases what into the atmosphere?
support: Burning organic material, such as fossil fuels, releases carbon dioxide.

question: At which location is the earth hottest?
support: Earth is hottest at the Equator and gets cooler toward the poles. The differences in heating create huge convection currents in the troposphere. At the Equator, for example, warm air rises up to the tropopause. When it can’t rise any higher, it flows north or south.

question: What is the result of a reaction between sulfur trioxide and water?
support: Sulfur trioxide gas reacts with water to form sulfuric acid. This is an unfortunately common reaction that occurs in the atmosphere in some places where oxides of sulfur are present as pollutants. The acid formed in the reaction falls to the ground as acid rain.

question: What lines the lungs and helps sweep mucus and pathogens out of the lungs?
support: Charles Daghlian. Cilia lining the lungs help sweep mucus and pathogens out of the lungs . Public Domain.

question: What is the creation of a new species called?
support: The creation of a new species is called speciation . Most new species develop naturally. But humans have also artificially created new breeds and species for thousands of years.

question: Which type of energy holds atoms together?
support: Atoms are held together by a certain amount of energy called bond energy.

question: Lens faces can generally either be concave, or what, which is the opposite of concave?
support: One or both of the lens faces is part of a sphere and can be concave or convex.

question: Vinegar is an example of what type of acid?
support: Carboxylic acid is a carbonyl in which in which the carbon atom is bonded to an OH group on one side and either a carbon or hydrogen atom on the other. Carboxylic acids are weak acids, for example, vinegar.

question: The highest level of organization in ecology is known as what?
support: The biosphere consists of all the parts of Earth where life can be found. This is the highest level of organization in ecology. It includes all of the other levels below it. The biosphere consists of all the world’s biomes, both terrestrial and aquatic.

question: What type of organisms carry out their life processes through division of labor and have specialized cells that do specific job?
support: Multicellular organisms carry out their life processes through division of labor. They have specialized cells that do specific jobs.

question: The length of the route between two points is known as what?
support: Distance is the length of the route between two points.

question: Using less energy or using energy more efficiently are the basic methods of what?
support: There are two basic ways to conserve energy. You can use less energy. You can also use energy more efficiently.

question: What type of particles do acids release, by definition?
support: Acids are molecular compounds that release hydrogen ions.

question: A diagram that represents feeding relationships is also called what?
support: Food chains and food webs are diagrams that represent feeding relationships. Essentially, they show who eats whom. In this way, they model how energy and matter move through ecosystems.

question: Continental drift and mantle convection are supported by data originating where?
support: Seafloor spreading is a mixture different ideas and data. Continental drift and mantle convection are supported by bathymetric and magnetic data from the seafloor.

question: Where is the seafloor youngest?
support: Seafloor is youngest near the mid-ocean ridges and gets progressively older with distance from the ridge. Orange areas show the youngest seafloor. The oldest seafloor is near the edges of continents or deep sea trenches.

question: How are heat changes in chemical reactions measured?
support: Heat changes in chemical reactions are typically measured in joules rather than calories. The conversion between a joule and a calorie is shown below.

question: What is the smallest particle of an element that still has the properties of that element?
support: The smallest particle of an element that still has the properties of that element is the atom. All the atoms of an element are like one another, and are different from the atoms of all other elements.

question: Much of the damage from hurricanes may be caused by?
support: A hurricane is a large storm with high winds and heavy rains. Hurricanes develop from tropical cyclones. They form over warm ocean water. Much of the damage from hurricanes may be caused by storm surge.

question: Color blindness, hemophilia and muscular dystrophy are three x-linked what?
support: Color blindness, hemophilia and muscular dystrophy are three x-linked phenotypes.

question: In what kind of state are particles fixed in place relative to one another?
support: In the solid state, particles are fixed in place relative to one another. In the liquid and gas states, individual particles are free to move.

question: Space shuttles are reusable vehicles designed to get astronauts where?
support: Space shuttles are reusable vehicles for American astronauts to get into space.

question: What does urine leave the body through?
support: process in which urine leaves the body through a sphincter at the end of the urethra.

question: Wave cut platforms are level areas formed by what?
support: Wave-cut platforms are level areas formed by wave erosion. Since these platforms are above sea level, it means that either sea level was higher relative or the rock was lower.

question: What are the cell walls of fungi made of?
support: The cell walls of fungi are made of chitin. Chitin is a tough carbohydrate that also makes up the outer skeleton of insects. The cell walls of plants are made of cellulose.

question: How many embryonic cell layers do flatworms have?
support: Flatworms have three embryonic cell layers. They have a mesoderm layer in addition to ectoderm and endoderm layers. The mesoderm layer allows flatworms to develop muscle tissues so they can move easily over solid surfaces.

question: Particles in what state of matter do not experience any force of mutual attraction or repulsion?
support: Gas particles do not experience any force of attraction or repulsion with each other.

question: Each hemisphere of the cerebrum consists of four parts, called what?
support: Each hemisphere of the cerebrum consists of four parts, called lobes. Each lobe is associated with particular brain functions. Just one function of each lobe is listed here.

question: With what does an electromagnetic wave start?
support: An electromagnetic wave starts with a vibrating charged particle.

question: Where are ribosomes made?
support: The nucleolus is inside the nucleus, and is where ribosomes are made.

question: What is the term for particles composed of three quarks?
support: Particles that are composed of three quarks are called baryons.

question: What type of rocks form when magma cools and forms crystals?
support: Igneous rocks form when magma cools and forms crystals. These rocks can form at Earth’s surface or deep underground. Figure below shows a landscape in California’s Sierra Nevada that consists entirely of granite.

question: What is the term for the conversion of a liquid to its vapor below the boiling temperature of the liquid?
support: Evaporation is the conversion of a liquid to its vapor below the boiling temperature of the liquid.

question: What is the mass that is "lost" in fission or fusion actually converted to?
support: When the nucleus of a radioisotope undergoes fission or fusion, it loses a tiny amount of mass. What happens to the lost mass? It isn’t really lost at all. It is converted to energy. How much energy? . The change in mass is tiny, but it results in a great deal of energy.

question: What is mollusks complete digestive system called?
support: Mollusks also have a coelom, a complete digestive system, and specialized organs for excretion.

question: The production and transport of gametes is performed by what type of organs?
support: 46.3 Reproductive organs produce and transport gametes.

question: What transition occurs as heat is added or removed from a substance?
support: Phase transitions occur as heat is added or removed from a substance.

question: What are the physical properties of water and carbon dioxide affected by?
support: The physical properties of water and carbon dioxide are affected by their polarities.

question: What part of the cell holds cell organelles in place within the cytoplasm?
support: Crisscrossing the cytoplasm is a structure called the cytoskeleton . It consists of thread-like filaments and tubules. The cytoskeleton is like a cellular “skeleton. ” It helps the cell keep its shape. It also holds cell organelles in place within the cytoplasm.

question: What mineral is stored and is maintained at normal levels in blood by the skeletal system?
support: The skeletal system stores calcium and helps maintain normal levels of calcium in the blood. Bones take up and store calcium when blood levels of calcium are high. They release some of the stored calcium when blood levels of calcium are low.

question: What type of isotope can be used to treat diseases like cancer?
support: Radioactive isotopes are also used in the treatment of certain diseases, such as cancer. These isotopes are administered to only the diseased tissue, with the goal of destroying the unhealthy cells.

question: What is the density needed to just halt universal expansion called?
support: critical density, the density needed to just halt universal expansion.

question: What are organic molecules that consist of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen called?
support: Carbohydrates are organic molecules that consist of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. They are made up of repeating units called saccharides. They provide cells with energy, store energy, and form structural tissues.

question: What is the term for small streams?
support: Small streams often flow into bigger streams or rivers. The small streams are called tributaries . A river and all its tributaries make up a river system.

question: What converters are used on motor vehicles to break down pollutants in exhaust to non-toxic compounds?
support: Catalytic converters are used on motor vehicles. They break down pollutants in exhaust to non-toxic compounds. For example, they change nitrogen oxides to harmless nitrogen and oxygen gasses.

question: Where do two tributaries come together at?
support: A tributary begins at its headwaters on one side of a divide. Two tributaries come together at a confluence.

question: What are the substances that the body needs for energy, building materials, and control of body processes?
support: Nutrients are substances that the body needs for energy, building materials, and control of body processes.

question: What has large crystals because the magma began to cool slowly, then erupted?
support: This sarcophagus is housed at the Vatican Museum. The rock is the igneous extrusive rock porphyry. Porphyry has large crystals because the magma began to cool slowly, then erupted.

question: What are nekton animals able to do in water?
support: Nekton are aquatic animals that can move on their own by “swimming” through the water. They may live in the photic or aphotic zone. They feed on plankton or other nekton. Examples of nekton include fish and shrimp.

question: What are large collections of millions or billions of stars called?
support: Galaxies are collections of millions to many billions of stars.

question: What do we call cyclones that form in tropical latitudes?
support: Hurricanes are cyclones that form in tropical latitudes. They are called tropical cyclones.

question: A wheel with a rope wrapped around it, hanging over a building, is an example of what type of machine?
support: This rusty iron wheel has a rope wrapped around it. The wheel and rope hang over a building. Together they make up a type of machine called a pulley.

question: Trees release what gas as a byproduct of photosynthesis, thereby facilitating human respiration?
support: Recall that trees release oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis. And you need oxygen to breathe. Do you know why? So your cells can perform cellular respiration and make ATP.

question: Which way does an electric charge always move from?
support: An electric charge flows when it has electric potential energy due to its position in an electric field. An electric charge always moves spontaneously from a position of higher to lower potential energy.

question: What kind of attraction does electrical force have?
support: The electrical force is a vector quantity that is positive in repulsion and negative in attraction.

question: What is the visible surface of the sun called?
support: The photosphere is the visible surface of the Sun ( Figure below ). It's the part that we see shining. Surprisingly, the photosphere is also one of the coolest layers of the Sun. It is only about 6,000°C.

question: In comparison to light, the speed of sound is faster or slower?
support: Figure 17.8 When a firework explodes, the light energy is perceived before the sound energy. Sound travels more slowly than light does. (credit: Dominic Alves, Flickr).

question: Which glands produce milk after the birth of offspring?
support: All female mammals have mammary glands. Mammary glands are glands that produce milk after the birth of offspring. Producing milk for offspring is called lactation. The colt in Figure below is getting milk from its mother.

question: Reduction often involves the gain of hydrogen, the loss of oxygen, or the gain of what?
support: Reduction often involves the gain of hydrogen, the loss of oxygen, or the gain of electrons.

question: What phylum includes sponges, which are aquatic invertebrates?
support: Sponges are aquatic invertebrates in Phylum Porifera. Sponges have specialized cells and an endoskeleton, but they lack tissues and body symmetry. Many live on coral reefs and have symbiotic relationships with other reef species.

question: An alpha particle, which is emitted during alpha decay, consists of two protons and what else?
support: A: Along with another electron, it can combine with an alpha particle to form a helium atom. An alpha particle, which is emitted during alpha decay, consists of two protons and two neutrons.

question: When small particles, such as clay and silt, are in mixed in water but do not disolve in the water, what state are they in?
support: Small particles, such as clay and silt, are carried in suspension . They are mixed throughout the water. These particles are not dissolved in the water.

question: What occurs when two free radicals come in contact with each other?
support: Termination occurs whenever two free radicals come in contact with one another (not shown). The two free electrons form a covalent bond and the free radical on each molecule no longer exists.

question: What requirement of the second circuit does the current that flows in the primary circuit depend on?
support: The current that flows in the primary depends on how much current is required by the secondary circuit.

question: Insects use what structures, located on the head, to smell and taste chemicals, and in some cases to hear sounds?
support: The head has a pair of antennae. Insects use their antennae to smell and taste chemicals. Some insects can also use their antennae to hear sounds.

question: What is the term for the measurement of the amount of variation of species in a given area?
support: Biodiversity is a measurement of the amount of variation of the species in a given area.

question: How often do partial lunar eclipses occur?
support: Partial lunar eclipses occur at least twice a year, but total lunar eclipses are less common. The Moon glows with a dull red coloring during a total lunar eclipse.

question: Genetic variation produced in sexual life cycles contributes to what process?
support: 13.4 Genetic variation produced in sexual life cycles contributes to evolution.

question: The jejunum is about 0.9 meters (3 feet) long (in life) and runs from the duodenum to the ileum. jejunum means “empty” in latin and supposedly was so named by the ancient greeks who noticed it was always what?
support: In relaxed muscle, the myosin-binding site on actin is blocked by ________. titin b. troponin c. myoglobin d. tropomyosin 17. The cell membrane of a muscle fiber is called a ________. myofibril b. sarcolemma c. sarcoplasm d. myofilament.

question: What parts of a human possess the highest concentration of thermoreceptors?
support: Thermoreceptors perceive sensations related to the temperature of objects. There are two basic categories of thermoreceptors: hot receptors and cold receptors. The highest concentration of thermoreceptors can be found in the face and ears.
